Cork University Hospital has lifted its restrictions on recruitment after a leaked letter.
The HSE chief executive has acknowledged that working relationships at CUH have broken down after a row over a leaked meeting, and says trust must be rebuilt.
Anne O'Connor has called for Andy Phillips to resign over his comments.

Micheál Martin "categorically denied" any instruction (A), nothing says restrictions were lifted (B), and she "had confidence in Mr Phillips" (D).

The minutes misrepresented what he actually said.

2026-11-16.q: Why does the writer mention that staff "fear being recorded"?
opts: To suggest that the leaked recording should be published in full.
To show that Ms O'Connor approved of the recording being made.
To explain why Mr Phillips apologised for his comments.

2026-11-16-2.q: What is the passage mainly about?
opts: US tariffs causing a recession in Ireland's domestic economy.
Ibec's forecast that Irish domestic demand will grow strongly next year despite volatile energy costs and rising interest rates.
The IMF's warning that Ireland's economy is about to slow sharply.
A record fall in employment caused by artificial intelligence.
2026-11-16-2.exp: The passage opens: "Irish domestic demand is projected to increase by 4% next year, notwithstanding volatile energy costs and rising interest rates", and Ibec says the economy "remains fundamentally sound". Tariffs hit headline GDP, not the domestic economy (A); the IMF warning is about "global resilience" (C); employment is expected to near "a record level" (D).

2026-11-16-2.q: What can be inferred from the contrast between domestic demand and headline GDP?
opts: Domestic demand is a less reliable measure than GDP.
Household savings have fallen sharply this year.
Ibec expects both measures to fall this year.
Headline GDP can give a misleading picture of conditions in Ireland because it is heavily affected by multinational activity.
2026-11-16-2.exp: Domestic demand "excludes the substantial distortions generated by multinational corporations" and is set to grow about 3.5%, while "headline GDP is expected to decline by 0.8%". The two move in opposite directions, so GDP does not reflect domestic conditions well. Savings are "considerable" (B), and domestic demand grows (C); (A) reverses the point.

2026-11-16-2.q: Which best describes the tone of the outlook as reported?

Deeply pessimistic and alarmed.
Indifferent to the risks facing the economy.
Angry about government spending plans.

It is not alarmed (B), it notes risks (C), and the National Development Plan is cited positively (D).

opts: Ireland has more healthy peatland than any other country.
Ireland will provide the full 100 billion dollars in funding.
Ireland's own large-scale restoration experience gives it expertise to share with other countries.

2026-11-16-3.q: Why does the writer state that peatlands cover only 3–4% of the planet's land but hold up to one third of soil carbon?
opts: To argue that peatlands are too small to matter for climate policy.
To show that peatlands are far more important for carbon storage than their size suggests.
To explain why Ireland has so much peatland.
To criticise the targets of the Peatland Breakthrough as too ambitious.
